symptoms: A task fails naming a file that the plan expected to read
The message often suggests refreshing the table cache
Re-running the job sometimes succeeds without any change
likely_causes: The file was deleted between the moment the plan listed it and the moment a task read it -- a concurrent writer, a compaction, or a retention job
The catalog or the table metadata points at a location whose contents changed underneath
A previous run left the listing cached and the underlying prefix moved on
diagnostic_steps: Read the listing of the prefix the plan targeted, and check whether the count of files is compatible with what the plan expected
Read whether another process writes to or maintains the same location while this job runs -- this failure is almost always about two writers on one clock
Separate a file that never existed from a file that stopped existing: the first is a metadata problem, the second is a concurrency one
fixes: Serialise the job against the process that maintains the location, so the listing does not move under the read
Refresh the table metadata before the read when the location is known to change
Use a table format that gives the reader a consistent snapshot, when concurrent maintenance is a permanent condition
unsafe_fixes: Retrying until it passes, which turns a correctness question into a timing one and hides the concurrent writer
Ignoring missing files by configuration, which makes the job succeed with less data than it should have read
verification: Row count of the output against the expected count at the source, for the same window. This failure has a silent sibling -- a read that succeeds with fewer files than it should have -- and only the count catches it
rollback: Restore the previous scheduling or metadata handling. If a run completed with partial data, the output is wrong and has to be reprocessed, not just reverted
